exhibit.title: First LAN test record
exhibit.text:
PC-A: 192.168.10.10, mask 255.255.255.0
PC-B: 192.168.10.20, mask 255.255.255.0
Both PCs connect to the same switch.
PC-A ping to 192.168.10.20: replies received

prompt: What does the successful test establish?
options: PC-A received ICMP replies from PC-B during this test.
PC-A can reach Internet destinations through the switch.
Every application on PC-B is available to PC-A.
The switch has saved the PCs’ addresses in startup configuration.
explanation: A successful ping proves only that ICMP echo replies came back from that address during the test. It says nothing about the Internet, other applications or saved configuration.

whyWrong.1: No Internet destination or router path was tested.
whyWrong.2: Ping tests ICMP only, not every service on the destination.
whyWrong.3: A ping does not read any device’s saved configuration.

exhibit.title: Context help
exhibit.text:
S1# show ip interface brief ?
  |     Output modifiers
  <cr>

prompt: What does `<cr>` in this context-help response mean?
options: Enter can complete the command here.
Enter will display another page of output.
explanation: `<cr>` stands for carriage return: the command is complete as typed and Enter runs it. Other listed items are optional extensions.

whyWrong.0: Context help only lists valid choices; it does not run the command.
whyWrong.1: `<cr>` means no further argument is required at this point.
whyWrong.3: The --More-- pager is separate from context help.

prompt: Which command saves the active configuration to the normal startup configuration?
explanation: The copy command takes the source first and the destination second. `copy running-config startup-config` saves the active configuration.

whyWrong.0: The source and destination are reversed, so this does not save the active configuration.
whyWrong.2: This displays the saved configuration; it does not update it.
whyWrong.3: This displays the active configuration; it does not save it.

prompt: On the classic IOS lab device, which two statements describe running and startup configuration? Choose two.
options: Running configuration contains only changes since the last save.
Running configuration represents the currently active settings.
Startup configuration changes whenever you enter end.
Startup configuration supplies saved settings for a normal boot.
Displaying startup configuration copies it into running configuration.
explanation: Running configuration is the active set of settings in RAM; startup configuration is the saved copy the device loads at boot. Leaving configuration mode or displaying a file copies nothing.

whyWrong.0: Running configuration holds all active settings, not just the unsaved difference.
whyWrong.2: `end` only changes command mode; saving needs a copy command.
whyWrong.4: A show command only displays the saved settings; it does not apply them.

prompt: Both PCs share one switch LAN. Which correction matches the supplied plan?
options: Keep both addresses because their subnet masks match.
Enter PC-A’s address as PC-B’s default gateway.
Rename PC-B’s workspace label without changing its address.
explanation: Each host on a LAN needs its own address, and PC-B repeats PC-A’s. Change PC-B to the assigned 192.168.10.20.

whyWrong.0: Matching masks do not make a duplicate host address valid.
whyWrong.1: A gateway setting does not remove the duplicate, and a same-LAN test needs no gateway.
whyWrong.3: A workspace label does not change the address configured on the host.

exhibit.title: Representative CLI excerpt
exhibit.text:
Switch> show running-config
             ^
% Invalid input detected at '^' marker.

prompt: Why is this command rejected on a default lab switch?
options: The display command belongs in global configuration.
The displayed command needs an interface selected first.
The command requires privileged EXEC on this device.
The hostname argument must follow running-config.
explanation: The > prompt is user EXEC, which cannot run `show running-config`. Enter `enable` to reach privileged EXEC first.

whyWrong.0: Global configuration is for changing settings; show running-config is a privileged EXEC command.
whyWrong.1: The whole running configuration is not displayed from an interface context.
whyWrong.3: A hostname is a setting inside the configuration, not an argument to this command.

exhibit.title: Separate device and project checks
exhibit.text:
Workspace label: S1
Saved project filename: 00-first-lan.pkt
Current CLI prompt: S1#

prompt: You need evidence that hostname S1 is in the switch’s startup configuration. Which additional check directly supplies it?
options: Find S1 in the workspace device label.
Close and reopen the CLI tab to read its prompt.
Find hostname S1 in show startup-config.
explanation: `show startup-config` displays the saved file, so it is the check that hostname S1 is saved. Running configuration, the prompt and workspace labels show only the active or simulator name.

whyWrong.0: The workspace label belongs to the simulator, not the IOS configuration.
whyWrong.1: Running configuration shows the active name, which may be unsaved.
whyWrong.2: The prompt shows the active name, not whether it was saved.

prompt: On which date does CCNA 200-301 v2.0 begin, according to this chapter?
explanation: The chapter states that v2.0 begins on 3 February 2027, the day after v1.1’s last testing day.

whyWrong.0: 2 February 2027 is the last testing day for v1.1.
whyWrong.2: 19 September 2026 is the date the exam information was checked.
whyWrong.3: 1 January 2027 is not a date Cisco gives for either version.

prompt: Where does a Cisco device keep its running configuration?
explanation: The running configuration is the active copy and lives in RAM, so a restart loses it unless you saved it.

whyWrong.0: NVRAM holds the startup configuration, the saved copy.
whyWrong.2: The .pkt file stores your project, not the device’s running configuration.
whyWrong.3: Flash holds software images, not the active configuration.

prompt: Which command or shortcut returns you from any configuration mode directly to privileged EXEC?
explanation: `end`, or the Ctrl+Z shortcut, returns from any configuration mode to privileged EXEC.

whyWrong.0: `exit` moves back only one configuration level.
whyWrong.2: `disable` leaves privileged EXEC for user EXEC and is not used from configuration mode.

prompt: Which global configuration command stops a lab switch from hanging after you mistype a command at an EXEC prompt?
explanation: IOS treats a mistyped word as a hostname and tries a DNS lookup, which hangs the prompt. `no ip domain-lookup` turns that lookup off.

whyWrong.1: `terminal length 0` turns off the --More-- pager, not the lookup.
whyWrong.3: Saving the configuration does not change how mistyped words are handled.
